name: English
headline: Learn the World's Languages Faster with AI.
intro: Turn YouTube into your personal language classroom. Use YouTube captions and automatic translations to learn from videos you love: read two languages side by side, replay each sentence, and keep the material that matters.
notice: Version 0.5.3 · Source preview · Build from source

labels.languageScope: 24 counts interface choices. Subtitle languages depend on the selected video's available tracks; it is not a promise of fluency in 24 languages.
labels.screenshotScope: Screenshots are captured from the actual 0.5.3 application. The screenshot's language is labeled separately from this document's language.
labels.license: MIT application license; third-party components retain their notices. AxonTube is not affiliated with YouTube, Google, or Apple.

steps.title: 1. Open YouTube
steps.body: Paste a video link. Available captions are requested automatically, with English first and Traditional Chinese second. Initial retrieval may take about 1–2 minutes; availability is not guaranteed.

steps.title: 2. Choose and practise
steps.body: Use the two visible subtitle dropdowns. Click a sentence to jump to it, replay it, or enable a sentence loop.

steps.title: 3. Save or export
steps.body: Save Video chooses a folder for accessible media and available subtitles. Export Bilingual Subtitles creates Word, TXT, or SRT from loaded captions.

steps.title: 4. Make it yours
steps.body: Change interface language, playback speed, subtitle size, and each track's timing offset. The app remembers interface and subtitle-language choices.

features.title: Two independent subtitle tracks
features.body: English / Traditional Chinese defaults; choose from the current video's available originals and automatic translations. Successful first-track captions remain usable if the second track fails.

features.title: Sentence-focused practice
features.body: Sentence search, click-to-seek, previous / next, replay, looping, playback speed, and following the current sentence.

features.title: Video with synchronized subtitles
features.body: Saving stays available while captions load. Each operation creates a new folder for accessible video; timed SRT tracks and bilingual reading files are added when captions are available. Video-only saving is supported. Incomplete work stays in a .partial folder.

features.title: Word, TXT, and SRT export
features.body: Export available subtitles with timing offsets applied. Word and TXT pair text by time overlap. If only one track is loaded, its content can still be exported.

features.title: 24 localized interfaces
features.body: Menus, status messages, and the learning slogan switch languages together. Arabic and Hebrew support right-to-left layouts; subtitle content is not changed by switching the interface.

features.title: Local playback and clear controls
features.body: Open local media and subtitle files from the File menu. Disabled actions are dimmed with reasons; selected modes have highlights and checkmarks; saving shows a busy state.

highlights.title: A short path from watching to practising
highlights.body: Four toolbar actions keep the main flow direct: YouTube → Save Video → Subtitles → Language. No extra caption-fetch button is needed.

highlights.title: Learning material you can keep
highlights.body: Timed captions and readable Word / TXT files support both listening practice and later review. Exports use new destinations and preserve original files.

highlights.title: Local work, no AI API key
highlights.body: Local media and saved subtitles work offline. YouTube supplies website captions and automatic translations; the app has no telemetry and does not upload local media or require a paid AI API key.

issues.title: YouTube caption and video availability
issues.body: The latest live check hit YouTube's sign-in / bot-verification requirement. Successful current online downloads have not been established. Validate under the intended network and across representative videos before public release.

issues.title: Embedding and account-restricted videos
issues.body: Some authors or videos disallow embedded playback. In-app Google SSO is not implemented; the browser shortcut uses a separate login and playback session. These restrictions cannot be presented as solved.

issues.title: Signing and broader Mac testing
issues.body: The package is ad-hoc signed, without Developer ID notarization. Apple Silicon on macOS 26.5.2 was tested; macOS 27 and Intel Macs were not. macOS 14 is a deployment target, not proof that every version has been tested.

issues.title: Download quality and subtitle fidelity
issues.body: Saving uses a complete audio/video stream and does not merge separate high-resolution streams. ASS/SSA imports text only. Automatic captions, translations, and timing-based bilingual pairing may contain errors. Local playback depends on codec support; optional FFmpeg conversion may omit extra audio tracks, HDR, and embedded subtitles.

issues.title: Learning-history and study tools
issues.body: Playback-history restoration, vocabulary collections, spaced review, OCR, and image-subtitle extraction are not implemented. Saved language preferences are not saved learning progress.

issues.title: Native-speaker language review
issues.body: All 24 interface choices and localized slogans passed switching checks. That establishes coverage and behavior, not professional native-speaker review of every translation.

evidenceSummary: For 0.5.3: 105 core checks, 138 model assertions, 29 caption checks, 60 video-save checks, and 317 native-interface assertions passed. All 24 language choices were selected in the actual menu; six interface languages and compact German layouts were reviewed.
evidenceLimit: Local playback, exports, state transitions, and native save dialogs were verified. Offline fixtures and fake-helper save tests do not prove that YouTube currently permits online caption or video downloads. No user credentials were imported.
